author: Ben Sample <ben@northwind.example>
title: The consultant's offer
text:
Hello Ada,

Thank you for the call on Wednesday. As promised, here is our offer for the consultant who would support your harbour site through the next quarter. We have looked at the robot arm rollout, the pallet labelling problems and the scanner firmware, and we believe one experienced consultant can cover all three with the help of your team. The plan starts with two weeks on site, then moves to weekly visits and a remote check every morning. During the first two weeks the consultant maps every station, measures how long each pallet waits, and writes down where the labels fail. After that the visits focus on training the shift leads and on the firmware updates, so that the night shift can handle a scanner fault without calling anyone.

The rollout of the robot arm needs the most attention. The arm itself is reliable, but the pick list it receives from the warehouse system is often late, and then the arm waits while the trucks wait behind it. The consultant would sit with your planners for the first days and change how the pick lists are cut, so that the arm always has the next three orders in hand. We have done the same at two other sites, and both saw the waiting time drop by a third within a month. We would also like to set up a short daily report, one page, that shows the arm's idle minutes, the late pick lists and the pallets that needed a hand label.

On the price: the day rate is four hundred thousand forints, and with twenty-five days in the quarter the total comes to ten million forints, travel included. Invoices go out monthly, each with the days worked and a short note of what was done. If a week is cancelled with five working days notice there is no charge for it. We can lower the total by moving some of the weekly visits to remote sessions, which would save about a fifth of the days, but we do not recommend it for the first month, when most of the work happens on the floor.

For the training we suggest three short sessions per shift rather than one long day, because the floor cannot spare people for long. Each session covers one topic: clearing a scanner fault, printing a label by hand when the printer stops, and restarting the robot arm after an emergency stop. The consultant leaves a one-page card for each topic at every station, in English and in Hungarian, and checks a month later whether the cards are still used or need changing. The shift leads get a longer session on reading the daily report, so they can see which station is slowing the rest down and act on it before the morning meeting. We have kept the sessions short on purpose: in our experience people remember a ten-minute session held at their own station far better than a day in a meeting room, and the cards do the rest.

Please let me know by Friday whether the scope works for you, and we will send the contract the same day. If you would like a smaller scope, the labelling work alone would take about ten days and could start next week.

Best regards,
Ben
